recipes.name: Panettone Bread Pudding with Spiced Orange Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon Grand Marnier or other orange-flavored liqueur
2.5 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into bits
0.25 cup Grand Marnier or other orange-flavored liqueur

steps.text: Arrange panettone bread cubes to fit compactly into a buttered 2-quart casserole dish. Do not compress too tightly; set aside any leftover bread cubes.

Whisk 3 eggs and 1/2 cup sugar together until sugar is dissolved and mixture becomes light yellow in color. Pour in cream, vanilla, and 1 tablespoon orange liqueur; whisk to combine. Stir in pinch of salt, 1/8 teaspoon nutmeg, lemon zest, and orange zest: pour mixture over panettone cubes in the casserole dish. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Remove bread pudding from the refrigerator, uncover, and dot the top of with 2 1/2 tablespoons butter; sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of white sugar.

Set casserole dish into a shallow pan that is 2 to 3 inches larger in diameter than the casserole dish. Set these pans onto the center rack of the preheated oven. Pour hot water into the outside pan, until it reaches a depth of 1 inch around the casserole dish, creating a water bath.

Bake the pudding in the water bath until it is fully set and a knife inserted into the center of the pudding comes out clean, 1 to 1 1/4 hours. The water bath will help the pudding to cook evenly and maintain a light texture. Carefully remove the pudding from the water bath and cool for at least 15 minutes before serving.

Just before serving, make the sauce by melting 1/2 cup butter in a saucepan over low heat. Stir in 1 cup sugar, 1/4 cup orange liqueur, 3 tablespoons water, 1/8 teaspoon nutmeg, and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Stir and heat over medium heat until the sugar is fully dissolved and the liquid is heated through. Remove from heat.

In a small mixing bowl, whisk 1 egg until well beaten. While whisking the egg, slowly pour 2 tablespoons of the hot mixture into the bowl with the egg. Then, while whisking mixture vigorously, slowly pour the warmed egg mixture back into the sauce.

Place the saucepan back over low heat, gently stirring the sauce and raising the temperature slowly to medium. Continue to stir until the sauce almost reaches a simmer, reducing the heat as necessary if the mixture threatens to boil. Continue stirring until the sauce thickens, 1 to 2 minutes. Spoon over the bread pudding and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Panettone Bread Pudding with Spiced Orange Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Panettone bread pudding is a great recipe to make if you're lucky enough to have any leftover panettone! Serve as a dessert or a decadent breakfast.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is so wonderful. Panettone certainly is the perfect bread for bread pudding. I also use it Christmas morning to make french toast with our leftover egg nog.

Absolutely delicious! I've made bread pudding many different ways with various liquors, but so far this is my favorite. I used Orange Panettone with Chocolate Chips and another brand of orange liquor. I had a 35oz panettone so I tripled the recipe and used 2 large glass pans to bake in the water bath. I cut the sugar in the sauce by half, added orange juice instead of water and a little cinnamon since I like that better than just nutmeg. The orange flavor with little bits of melted chocolate perfectly complemented eachother. I'm going to make again using Lemon Panettone and Limoncello.

Although the flavor was good, and the bread was delicious, this bread pudding was a little too sweet for my taste. Also, I like bread pudding to be more custardy, which requires the addition of more eggs. If I make it again, I will try it with less sugar.
Made this in slow cooker - 3 hours on low.

This was such a huge hit to New Year's Day dinner. I doubled the recipe and made it in a small roasting pan. When I took the pork roast out this went in. One thing I did was make it with the panettone with chocolate chips in it because they were out of the regular citrus bread. OH. MY. GOODNESS! The orange and chocolate was such a great combination. Based on other reviews about the sweetness with the sauce I decided to provide a bowl of fresh whipped cream if anyone wanted to top it. It was GREAT!

This is delicious! I tried to follow the recipe but accidentally added 1/4 tsp nutmeg each time instead of 1/8 tsp and also 1/4 tsp salt instead of 1/8. Also I cut down the sugar in the sauce to only 1/4 cup. I probably used closer to 16 oz + of panettone instead of 12 oz. there is plenty of room in the 2 quart roasting pan to probably use almost a whole 26 oz loaf. The bread pudding rises but will deflate to about 1/3It’s sooooo goood!!!! It’s going to go great with Christmas dinner. I’m going to make another ASAP!

I made this January 1 and it was sooooo good! Here are the changes that I made- 2 TBSP of sugar only- people- you dont need to use a ton of sugar! 2-1/4 cups 5% cream because I didnt have half and half, I used 1 TBSP orange extract because I didn't have Grand Marnier or other, ground cloves instead of nutmeg, no orange zest either, and no butter on top- but I did need to use and extra egg- cooked this at 350 for 1-1/2 hours without using the hot water bath method and it turned out fantastic!!!

This is a great recipe, thoughtfully planned and accurate directions. It came out amazing. One half of a leftover store bought panettone was 13 oz. and it fit perfectly in the casserole dish. I subbed orange juice because I had no liquor (omitted the added water). I loved this so much I will probably make it again and again, but might try subbing some lighter ingredients because it is SO rich.
I'd give it a five, but I add more spices to mine, no sugar and added coconut chunks, raisins, cranberries and topped with pecan. Sometimes don't do the sauce and top with agave for a healthier kick!
this is a terrific way to make bread pudding. the only thing I did differently was I used raw Agave Nectar in place of the white sugar in the pudding and the sauce and it was spot on delicious

This has become my go-to recipe for all types of bread but it is especially good with panettone because of its light texture. I do refrigerate my bread puddings overnight before baking, not just for the 30 minutes recommended in this recipe. Make with any panettone, traditional, coffee cream, chocolate chip, etc. I serve without the sauce.
This is a delicious and easy recipe. My husband loved it even though he typically does not like bread pudding.

We followed the recipe to the letter and it turned out beyond all of our expectations! We made it just before midnight on Christmas Eve because enjoying Panettone was part of my friend's Peruvian Christmas Tradition, but they had never made bread pudding out of it before. It was moist and delicious and the Grand Marnier sauce was to die for. I hope you enjoy it as much as we did!

Made this over the holidays (posting my review a little late sorry). It is perfect for my family as we are half British and half Italian. The combination was awesome and festive. It made an excellent Christmas morning breakfast. Will be sure to make this every year from now on in.
This bread pudding is to die for. I look forward to it every christmas.

I wanted to like this BUT I didn't. It baked well, was the consistency that I was hoping for but it tasted too much like fruit cake. It had this taste/flavor that was NOT appealing...to me. Plenty of people may like fruit cake and this is for them. I will try this again with a different bread.
My friend replaces the cream with eggnog...epic!
Awesome bread pudding!!!

This was the best! Even though I had to punt on some of the ingredients. I used Amaretto instead of Grand Marnier, a bit short of nutmeg, so I added some of Penzey's cake seasoning. All the rest was the same. the recipe was easy to follow. And the sauce! I had all of my ingredients ready on the counter, and when we were finished with our meal, I put the sauce together, right in front of the guests. Again I substituted Amaretto and the cake spice for the required ingredients. Yummy! I will definitely be making this again!!!!

As written this is WAY too sweet... and listen, I LOVE sweets! I did like the panettone bread used in a bread pudding, and may use the bread again in one of my regular bread puddings, but definitely not with this sticky sweet syrup on top. I didn't even use all the sauce and think I may need to mix it with some milk or something to even use it on anything else... WAY TOO SWEET!
